Kuvitus: betonipato vuoristolaaksossa si: Illustration: a concrete dam in a mountain valley seen from the side. Behind the dam is a deep reservoir whose water gets darker with depth. The dam is narrow at the top and widens downwards; at the bottom it is many times thicker.
Illustration: a diver deep in a lake. The water gets darker with depth, air bubbles rise to the surface, and the diver wears a depth and pressure gauge on the wrist.
Sama voima F kohdistuu samanlaiseen tiil: The same force F acts on an identical brick in two ways. On the left the brick stands on end and touches the ground with a small area A1, so the pressure p1 = F/A1 is large. On the right the brick lies on its side and touches the ground with an area three times as large, A2 = 3 A1, so the pressure p2 = F/A2 is one third of the pressure on the left. The force arrows are equally long. The contact areas are to scale; the diagram is otherwise schematic.
Vesipatsas, jonka pohjan pinta-ala on A: A column of water whose base has area A and whose height is the depth h. The weight of the column, G = ρAhg, presses the base downwards, and the pressure is the weight divided by the area, p = G/A = ρgh: the area cancels. Schematic diagram, not to scale.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: veden paine p kil: Graph to scale: the pressure p of water in kilopascals as a function of the depth h for h from 0 to 10 m. The pressure is a rising straight line: at the surface the pressure is atmospheric pressure, 101 kPa, and at a depth of 10 metres about 199 kPa. The gap between the line and the dashed line is the hydrostatic pressure ρgh.
